## Goal

As an operator reading `monitoring/README.md` I can find the new slot series, run
the utilisation CLI from a copy-pasteable example, understand the retention and
resolution limits of the store, and re-measure the power calibration myself after
a hardware, driver or kernel change.

## Context

Parent: LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W (AC7, AC8). The README already documents deployment,
the exposure boundary, the PromQL query cookbook and the "why not `amd-smi`"
evidence (LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL). This child adds the workload series, the CLI, the
retention/resolution statements and the calibration procedure, and closes the
documentation gap between the hardware figure (`gpu:computing:bool`) and the
usage report's proxy-inferred `local_busy.busy_pct`.

Two figures must not be conflated (see LP-0MVSPWLLP008AQXZ, which measured a ~27
point divergence): the log-derived figure measures slot occupancy from proxy
events, the hardware+slot figure measures "GPU drew compute power while at least
one slot was busy". The docs must state what each answers and why neither
replaces the other.

## Minimal implementation

- `monitoring/README.md`: extend the "What runs here" table and the query
  cookbook with `llama_slots_busy`, `llama_slot_busy`, `llama_slots_total`,
  `llama_slots_in_flight_tasks`, `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` and
  `gpu:computing_workload:bool`; add a CLI section with a real example run.
- New calibration subsection: idle ≈ 40–54 W, computing ≈ 115 W, threshold 90 W,
  and the re-measure recipe (`cat /sys/class/drm/card0/device/hwmon/hwmon*/power1_average`
  while idle and during a known-long generation; update the rule threshold and
  `server.llama_gpu_wedge_power_low_threshold_watts` together).
- Retention/resolution statement: 90 d, history starts when the TSDB was created
  (2026-10-25 19:22 on this host), observed resolution is the 15 s scrape interval
  even though the sysfs sampler writes at 10 s.
- Keep `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` accurate; update it only if the
  cadence/responsibilities actually change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Parent AC7 (restated in full):** Documentation is updated: `monitoring/README.md` gains the slot series, the CLI usage, the retention statement (90 d, and that history starts when the TSDB was created) and a calibration/re-measure section, plus an explicit note on how computing-time % differs from the usage report's proxy-inferred `local_busy.busy_pct`; code comments and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` stay accurate.
- [ ] **Parent AC8 (restated in full):** Full project test suite passes with the new changes via `/skill:test`.
- [ ] Documentation is updated: `monitoring/README.md` gains the slot series, the `gpu_utilisation.py` CLI usage, the retention statement (90 d, and that history starts when the TSDB was created) and a calibration/re-measure section, plus an explicit note on how computing-time % differs from the usage report's proxy-inferred `local_busy.busy_pct`; code comments and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` stay accurate.
- [ ] The documented CLI example is copy-pasteable and its output block matches the real column layout produced by the sibling CLI child (verify by running it, not by transcribing an intention).
- [ ] The calibration section states the measured idle/computing bands and the re-measure procedure precisely enough that a clean host can reproduce the numbers, including which sysfs file and which config keys carry the threshold.
- [ ] `gpu_busy_percent` appears in the README only in the "not a utilisation signal" context; a grep assertion in the existing docs test suite (or a new assertion) enforces it.
- [ ] `monitoring/README.md` states the resolution floor (15 s scrape, 10 s sysfs write) and that the CLI reports the step it queried, so no figure implies finer fidelity than the store holds.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes via `/skill:test`.
- [ ] Each of the parent's eight acceptance criteria is re-checked at completion against the shipped behaviour (a short pass/fail table in the completion comment links each criterion to the file or command that proves it), and any criterion the plan did not cover is raised as a comment on the parent instead of being quietly dropped.

**Key Files:**

- `monitoring/README.md`
- `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`
- `docs/systemd/node_exporter.service` (only if the textfile/sampler description drifts)
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` (doc assertions)

## Notes

This is the last slice: it documents what actually shipped, not the plan. If a
sibling child had to deviate (metric names, flag names, exit codes), the docs
follow the code and the deviation is recorded in the parent's plan changelog.

# Prove the dev-push gate refuses a failing skill test

## Goal

Enforcement is proven end-to-end: a deliberately failing test under
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` makes the dev-push full-suite gate
refuse, and removing it restores green (parent AC2). The repo/skill/combined
counts measured during the proof are published as three distinct numbers
(parent AC3, work-item half).

## Context

Parent: **LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X**. **Blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** — the gate
cannot refuse a skill-test failure until the upstream resolution rule emits the
extra explicit-path command.

## Minimal implementation

- On a scratch branch in the implementation worktree, add a deliberately
  failing test under `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests`
  (e.g. `test_gate_proof_tmp.py`).
- Force an **uncached** `--scope full` gate run: the runner caches per git
  state and command, so use a fresh git state or remove the matching
  `.worklog/cache` entry, and record which method was used.
- Capture the verbatim gate output excerpt that names the failing skill test
  and both suite commands, then remove the failing test and re-run uncached to
  confirm green.
- Never push the red tree to `origin/dev` (or `main`): use a scratch branch
  plus the documented stdin push simulation in `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` if a
  hook-level proof is wanted.

**Key Files:**

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/conftest.py`
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Enforcement proven end-to-end.** After SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB ships and
  its runner is installed, a deliberately failing test under
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` on a scratch branch makes the gate
  refuse the `dev` push (uncached run), and removing the test confirms green.
- **AC2 — Skill command named.** The same gate output lists both the canonical
  repo pytest command and the `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests` command,
  proving the skill suite is inside the gate's command set.
- **AC3 — Clean after removal.** After the failing test is removed, the same
  uncached run passes and the combined total is recorded.
- **AC4 — Counts published separately.** The repo-test count, the skill-test
  count and the combined total are published as three distinct numbers in a
  work-item comment together with the gate output excerpt.
- **AC5 — No red push.** No push of the red tree to `origin/dev` or `main` is
  attempted; the proof uses a scratch branch and, if needed, the documented
  stdin simulation.


## Dependencies

- **Blocked by SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB** (cross-store).
- After the drift-guard test (test-first ordering).

## Deliverables

- Verbatim gate output excerpt in a work-item comment.
- Three published counts + the uncached-run method used.
- No committed code (the failing probe test is removed).

**and** project-local skill tests, the split counts, the measured runtime, and
the rule that this repo must not pin `suiteCommands` (parent AC3 documentation

Parent: LP-0MVRBQBDF0037OZ5 (Compact before moving from local to remote). Covers parent AC7.

**Goal:** As a proxy maintainer (and as the operator who must be able to switch this on safely), I want the local→remote boundary compaction documented — its trigger, its own knob, its release ordering and its fail-open behaviour — so enabling it needs no code reading and its relationship to the disabled assembly-time compaction is unambiguous.

**Target outcome:** the operator-facing and developer-facing docs describe the boundary trigger and exactly how to enable, tune and disable it.

**Minimal implementation**

1. `docs/llama-router.md` — a "Boundary compaction (local → remote)" subsection under the session-compaction section: when it fires (remote provider + recorded local provenance + size guard), the slot it uses, the immediate release, the fail-open WARNING tokens, the latency cost and the `X-Compaction-*` mirroring.
2. `proxy/config.yaml` — `remote_boundary_compaction: false` and `remote_boundary_compaction_min_tokens` with explanatory comments stating explicitly that these do **not** re-enable `compaction_trigger_ratio` (which stays `0` per the operator's 2026-09-17 decision, LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6).
3. Module docstrings: `compaction.decide_boundary_compaction`, the slot-pinned summariser builder, and `router_helpers.evaluate_boundary_compaction` — trigger, tokens, KV caveat, why there is no remote summariser fallback.
4. A short "what changed vs LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6" note so a future reader does not mistake this for a re-enable of assembly-time compaction.

**Definition of done**

- Pass/fail checks
  - A reader can enable the feature from `docs/llama-router.md` alone (knob name, default, guard, expected log lines).
  - The doc names all four WARNING reason tokens and what each means operationally.
  - `proxy/config.yaml` comments state the independence from `compaction_trigger_ratio` and link the disable decision.
  - Docstrings match the implemented behaviour (verified while writing them).
- Automated tests: no new tests; the docs-only change must not alter behaviour (existing doc-lint / config-load tests stay green).

**Constraints**

- UK English; match the existing documentation tone and heading levels.
- Do not restate or edit the assembly-time compaction design docs beyond a cross-reference.
- No behaviour change in this item.

**Risky assumptions**

- None material: the documentation follows the implemented behaviour from the preceding items. If the implementation deviates from the plan (e.g. one call site instead of two), the doc describes what was built and notes the deviation.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/llama-router.md` — boundary-compaction section.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — knob + guard comments.
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py`, `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — module docstrings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `docs/llama-router.md` (compaction section) documents the boundary trigger, its knob and the immediate slot release along with its fail-open behaviour.
2. The new config keys are documented with explanatory comments in `proxy/config.yaml`, shipping disabled by default and stating that they do not re-enable assembly-time compaction.
3. Module docstrings describe the boundary trigger, its fail-open WARNING reason tokens and the slot-reuse KV caveat.
4. An operator can enable, tune and revert the feature from the documentation alone, and the relationship to `LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6` (assembly-time compaction disabled) is stated explicitly.

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want one inventory table of every routing/balancing
mechanism and metric on the local dispatch path showing its 2-slot value, its
1-slot value and a derived/static verdict, so I cannot switch geometry and
silently keep 2-slot routing behaviour (parent AC1, AC2).

## Approach

1. Create `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` with the section skeleton: verdict,
   inventory table, throughput prediction (sibling item fills it), metrics gaps
   (sibling item fills it), method and provenance, citations appendix.
2. Walk the dispatch path and fill one row per mechanism: `value @ 2 slots`,
   `value @ 1 slot`, classification (`derived-auto` /
   `static-needs-manual-change` / `not-applicable`), `file:line` evidence.
3. Take every derived number from the sibling test item's assertions rather
   than re-deriving by hand.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` exists with an inventory table covering
  at least: per-slot context; physical per-slot clamp; economic warm ceiling;
  absolute warm cap (`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`); cold
  threshold (`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`); hard-routing cap;
  `local_session_tenants`; the dispatch lease pool (`max_local`);
  `local_max_concurrent_prefills`; contention-queue wait / depth / lease grace
  / ETA ordering; slot-exhaustion retries
  (`local_slot_exhaustion_retry_attempts`, `_retry_delay_seconds`); `/health`
  and `/llama/local/status` slot counts plus per-slot detail; the
  usage-analysis report metrics (local busy %, turns served locally,
  input/output tokens processed locally, diverts by reason, queue waits,
  dispatch-to-first-byte, prefill and decode slot-seconds, decode tok/s); the
  Prometheus `llama_slots_*` counters; herdr's consumption of the status
  endpoint.
- AC2: Every row records all four fields, and each classification is one of the
  three canonical values; each row cites `file:line` (or an endpoint plus the
  emitting module) as evidence.
- AC3: The report states the headline answer explicitly: how many inventory
  items auto-adjust, which items stay static, and the exact `key: old -> new`
  list a coherent single-slot switch requires — including that the explicit
  `local_session_tenants: 2` in `proxy/config.yaml:1386` does not follow the
  slot count even though its documented default would, and that
  `handlers.py` falls back to a stale default of 3 slots.
- AC4: The report states explicitly that the absolute warm cap (120000) and the
  economic ratio (0.4578) hold the effective warm ceiling at 120000 even though
  the physical per-slot clamp doubles to 258048, so doubling the per-slot
  context routes nothing extra on its own.
- AC5: No hand-computed number appears without a citation: each is either
  pinned by the sibling test item (referenced by test name) or cites
  `file:line` / a measured baseline with its window.
- AC6: The one-line verdict is recorded as a comment on the parent
  LP-0MVTF26NP003KXKJ.
- AC7: The report states its scope boundaries — prediction plus
  auto-adjustment audit, not the geometry verdict (which stays with the A/B
  LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN) — and that no runtime behaviour changed in this work.

**Parent AC1 trace:** the inventory table in `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md`
with value @2 / value @1 / classification / `file:line` for every listed
mechanism and metric.
**Parent AC2 trace:** headline counts, the static items listed by name, the
exact `key: old -> new` list, the warm-ceiling/absolute-cap statement, and the
verdict comment on the parent.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` - the new report (main deliverable)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` - threshold, cap, lease-pool and slot-count derivations
- `proxy/config.yaml` - slot, context, threshold and queue keys with their comments
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` - `/slots` counts, per-slot detail, status payload
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` - `/llama/local/status` and `/health` consumers
- `proxy/proxy/capacity_admission.py` - slot-pool sizing helper
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` - local concurrency reads of the slot pool
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` - Prometheus `llama_slots_*` counters
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` - report metric catalogue

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the test item (derived numbers must be pinned first).
- Blocks the throughput-prediction slice, which reuses the classifications.

## Deliverables

- `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` with the verdict section, the inventory
  table and the report skeleton for the sibling slices.
- The one-line verdict comment on the parent work item.

## Goal (user story)

As the pipeline owner, I want a reasoned, quantified prediction of what one
slot does to turns and tokens served locally over time, so I can tell whether
fewer slots cost throughput or only latency (parent AC3).

## Approach

1. Add the "throughput impact" section to `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md`.
2. For each effect, state the mechanism, the sourced baseline (with its window
   and file), the predicted direction and rough magnitude at 1 slot, the metric
   that would confirm or refute it, and the A/B arm comparison
   (Arm A = 2 x 131,072 vs Arm B = 1 x 262,144, protocol in
   `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md`).
3. State the token-attribution rule explicitly before quoting any token count.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The report predicts, at request level, each of: turns served locally;
  tokens processed locally (prompt and completion); per-session first-byte and
  decode latency; head-of-line blocking and queue waits; slot reuse / thrash and
  the resulting re-prefill volume; and concurrency headroom.
- AC2: Each conclusion names (a) the mechanism in code or config with
  `file:line`, (b) its sourced baseline with the measurement window and source
  document, and (c) the metric plus the Arm A vs Arm B comparison that would
  confirm or refute it.
- AC3: Token figures state their provenance: the `Stream finished`
  `tokens=prompt/completion/total` lines are authoritative, any derived figure
  is labelled an estimate, the local-versus-remote turn split rule is stated,
  and the count of lines lacking token evidence in the baseline window is
  recorded.
- AC4: The report states the uncontended-evidence caveat — local was idle
  ~90 % of the baseline window and measured concurrency averaged ~1.04 while
  busy — so the serialisation cost of one slot is under-observed today and the
  prediction must not be presented as a measured result.
- AC5: The prediction is consistent with the inventory item's classifications:
  any effect that depends on a static knob is stated as conditional on the
  manual change listed in the `key: old -> new` list.
- AC6: Where a conclusion depends on a baseline that must be re-measured, the
  report says so and names the confirming measurement instead of asserting a
  number.

- AC7: AC3: a reasoned throughput-impact analysis at request level, including tokens processed locally.

**Parent AC3 trace:** request-level throughput-impact analysis including tokens
processed locally, with a named mechanism and a sourced baseline for every
conclusion, and a confirming metric plus A/B arm comparison for each.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` - the report section (main deliverable)
- `docs/dev/slot-reuse-gap-final-report.md` - re-prefill and prefix-reuse baselines
- `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` - the A/B arms, protocol and decision gate
- `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` - cache-preservation and thrash findings
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` - turn/token/divert/queue metric definitions
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` - `local_max_concurrent_prefills` and lease-pool behaviour
- `proxy/config.yaml` - queue caps, thresholds and their measured rationale

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the inventory item (classifications and the `old -> new` list).
- Blocks the metrics-gap slice, which enumerates a detection metric per
  conclusion.

## Deliverables

- The throughput-impact section of `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md`, with a
  provenance subsection for token accounting.
data.title: Predict single-slot throughput impact

## Goal (user story)

As on-call, I want the audit to say which existing metric would reveal
single-slot starvation and which ones would stay silent, with every blind spot
filed as follow-up work, so I know where the observability gaps are without
this item growing into a metrics implementation (parent AC4).

## Approach

1. Add a "metrics gaps" table to `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md`: one row per
   throughput conclusion from the sibling slice, with the existing metric that
   would detect it (or "none"), and whether it is sufficient.
2. For every gap, search for an existing work item first (notably the blocked
   slot-occupancy item LP-0MVT1O0VG00905EL) and only create a new one when the
   gap is genuinely uncovered, using `discovered-from:<parent>` linking.
3. Do not add metrics or change configuration values — gaps are filed, not
   implemented.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The report contains a gaps table with one row per single-slot
   conclusion from the throughput slice, each stating whether an existing
   metric can detect it, which metric, and the detection window needed.
- AC2: The report names the metrics that stay silent under a single-slot
   regime — at minimum the absence of published per-slot occupancy, since
   llama-server `/slots` detail is consumed only for counts and processing
   state.
- AC3: Every gap row is backed by either an existing open work item (id cited,
   linked as related work) or a newly created follow-up work item; no gap is
   left unfiled.
- AC4: Any new follow-up work item links back to this parent (child if
   blocking, otherwise `discovered-from:` in its description) and states the
   metric it would add plus how it would surface single-slot starvation.
- AC5: No new metric, endpoint field, or configuration value is implemented in
   this slice; the diff is documentation plus worklog items.

- AC6: AC4: a metrics-gap list: for each single-slot conclusion, state whether an existing metric can detect it.

**Parent AC4 trace:** a metrics-gap list stating per conclusion whether an
existing metric detects it, with every blind spot filed as follow-up work
rather than implemented here.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` - the gaps table (main deliverable)
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` - what `/slots` detail is and is not published
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` - the Prometheus counters that exist today
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` - `/health` and `/llama/local/status` payload fields
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` - the report metrics available today

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the throughput-prediction slice (its conclusions are the gap-table
  rows).

## Deliverables

- The metrics-gaps section of `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md`.
- Filed follow-up work items (or cited existing ones) for every blind spot.

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want the docs and code comments that assert a fixed 2-slot
pool corrected and cross-linked to the new report, so the next reader is not
told that two slots are structurally guaranteed (parent documentation AC).

## Approach

1. Add cross-links from the design/protocol docs to
   `docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md`.
2. Correct comments that assert a fixed 2-slot pool or a stale slot count,
   without changing any configuration value or runtime behaviour.
3. Leave factual, still-true statements alone; where a comment's intent is
   unclear, record an Open Question instead of rewriting it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` and `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`
   cross-link the new report and no longer describe 2 slots as structurally
   fixed where the slot count is in fact configurable.
- AC2: The comments that assert a fixed 2-slot pool are corrected:
   `proxy/config.yaml` (`session_slot_pool_size` rationale) and
   `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_effective_large_context_thresholds`, "the slot
   pool is fixed at 2").
- AC3: Stale slot-count comments/defaults found during the audit are either
   corrected (when unambiguous) or recorded as a follow-up work item —
   including the `_get_active_local_slots` docstring's "default/fast: 3,
   cheap: 2" and the `session_slot_pool_size` fallback default of `3` in
   `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`.
- AC4: `models.ini` launch-flag comments describing per-slot context reflect
   1-slot reality correctly (i.e. they describe per-slot context as derived
   from `local_model_ctx_size / slots`, so the comment is true at either
   count), and no launch flag or config value is changed.
- AC5: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` is cross-linked to the
   report and carries no assertion that a fixed 2-slot pool holds. (This file is
   explicitly in the parent work item's documentation AC, which is the
   authorisation for touching `.pi/`.)
- AC6: No configuration value changes in this slice: the diff is comments,
   documentation and cross-links only, verifiable by inspecting the diff for
   non-comment changes.
- AC7: The full project test suite passes with these changes (run through the
   test skill), as the terminal slice of this work item.

- AC8: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and docs entries.

**Parent documentation AC trace:** all related documentation updated, with
cross-links and fixed-2-slot assertions corrected in
`docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md`, `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`,
`proxy/config.yaml`, `models.ini` and
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`.
**Parent suite AC trace:** full project test suite passes with the new changes.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` - A/B protocol doc, cross-link and slot-count claims
- `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` - design doc, cache-preservation claims
- `proxy/config.yaml` - `session_slot_pool_size` and stale slot-count comments
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` - fixed-2-slot comment and `_get_active_local_slots` docstring
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` - stale slot-count fallback default
- `./models.ini` - launch-flag comments describing per-slot context
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` - analysis reference doc

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the inventory item (the report must exist to link to) and, in
  practice, by the metrics-gap slice so the corrections are made once.

## Deliverables

- Corrected comments and cross-links across the five named files.
- Follow-up work items for any ambiguous stale slot-count claim left alone.

# Resolve the model id from /models instead of hard-coding Qwen3 (AC2 part 2)

**Parent:** LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 · **Slice:** 4 of 6 · **Type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Summary

Replace the hard-coded `"Qwen3"` model default in the child-port discovery and slot-availability paths with a `/models`-derived id (case-insensitive preset match, `"Qwen3"` only as a logged last resort), and prove an unknown id fails open once rather than looping.

## Why this slice

The router's `/models` ids are presets, not one universal name (`Qwen3`, `mxbai-embed`, `Qwen2.5-7B`, `Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF:Q5_K_M`, …). A hard-coded default therefore sends an unresolvable `?model=` whenever the preset differs — a router 400 by construction. This slice completes AC2 and empties the guard-test allowlist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC2 — No model-less proxy `/slots`.** None of `backend_health.py:242`, `backends/llama.py:212`, `compaction_summarizer.py:55` issues `/slots` without `?model=`; each passes the resolved model or skips the query when no model is loaded. The hard-coded `"Qwen3"` defaults at `router_helpers.py:5570`/`:5795` are replaced by `/models`-derived resolution (default retained only as a documented last resort). The first sentence's call-site half landed in the predecessor slice LP-0MVU7ZZ7M002D9GT; this slice completes the AC and is the item that may mark it met.
- [ ] `_discover_local_child_port` and `_check_slot_availability` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`) no longer hard-code `"Qwen3"`; the target resolves as `srv.current_model` → the model id parsed from the live child-port log signal → a case-insensitive match against the router's `/models` ids/presets → `"Qwen3"` as a documented last resort.
- [ ] Resolution costs no extra `/models` HTTP round trip on the hot `/slots` path: the id snapshot is cached with a TTL consistent with the existing child-port cache and refreshed on a llama-server restart or model switch — asserted by a test showing a warm cache resolves the model id with zero `/models` HTTP requests.
- [ ] A test proves that when the router's `/models` reports a different preset id (e.g. `Qwen3-32B`), the emitted `?model=` is that id — not `"Qwen3"` — while the child port still comes from the log signal.
- [ ] A loop-guard test proves an unknown or alias-mismatched model produces exactly one fail-open result (0/0, with `http_400` still classified as the definite "model absent" signal by `slots_failure_is_definitive_model_absent`) and never a retry loop.
- [ ] The slice 2 guard-test allowlist is empty and the suite passes through the test skill's changed-scope gate.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the child-port signal scan to return the model id alongside the port, and use it as the primary resolution source (it is the id the router itself reports, so it is resolvable by definition).
- Add a small cached `/models` id snapshot built on the existing `router_list_models` / `_extract_router_model_ids` helpers in `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`; case-insensitive match, TTL mirroring `_child_port_cache_ttl()`.
- Log the resolved source (`current_model` / log signal / models snapshot / last-resort default) in the existing throttled child-port fallback warning.
- Preserve `slots_failure_is_definitive_model_absent` semantics and single-attempt behaviour; add the loop-guard assertion.
- Empty the guard-test allowlist.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_discover_local_child_port`, `_check_slot_availability`, `_scan_child_port_signals`, `_child_port_cache_ttl`
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `router_list_models`, `_extract_router_model_ids` (reuse)
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `slots_failure_is_definitive_model_absent` (semantics to preserve)
- `proxy/tests/test_child_port_discovery_rotation.py` — rotation/caching behaviour to keep green
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_model_param_guard.py` — allowlist to empty

## Dependencies

- Depends on: LP-0MVU7ZZ7M002D9GT (all model-less call sites thread a model id)

## Deliverables

- `/models`-derived model resolution with a cached snapshot, a model-switch test, a fail-open loop-guard test, and an empty guard-test allowlist.
data.title: Resolve the model id from /models instead of hard-coding Qwen3 (AC2 part 2, AC3b)

# Document the model-resolution rule and 400 semantics (AC5)

**Parent:** LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 · **Slice:** 5 of 6 · **Type:** docs · **Priority:** medium

## Summary

Document the model-resolution rule and the three distinct router `/slots` 400 classes in the operator-facing README and the triage doc, so an operator can tell a proxy defect from an expected "model not loaded" answer.

## Why this slice

The intake answer Q2 = A makes the unloaded-model 400 *expected truth*, which only holds if it is documented. Without this slice the guard tests enforce a rule that no operator-facing doc states.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC5 — Tests + docs.** Changed-scope and full project test suite pass (via the test skill); `proxy/README.md` and `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` document the model-resolution rule (`?model=` from `/models` ids/presets; router 400 semantics for *missing* vs *unknown* vs *unloaded* model).
- [ ] `proxy/README.md` documents the resolution order actually implemented (`srv.current_model` → live child-port log signal → `/models` id/preset match → `"Qwen3"` as a logged last resort) and that queries target the discovered child port.
- [ ] `proxy/README.md`'s existing "Child-port discovery (why `/slots` bypasses the router)" section is extended rather than duplicated.
- [ ] `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` documents the three 400 classes distinctly: *missing* `?model=` (proxy defect, fenced by the guard test), *unknown/unresolvable* id (proxy defect, resolved from `/models`), and *unloaded* model (expected truth, the definitive-model-absent signal the proxy fail-opens on).
- [ ] Both docs name the guard test so an operator can verify the rule is enforced, and link LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5 for the deferred per-query attribution.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the README child-port discovery section with a "Model resolution rule" subsection plus a short 400-class table.
- Add a "`/slots` 400 semantics" section to the triage doc, next to the existing responder-split evidence.
- Cross-reference `slots_failure_is_definitive_model_absent` and `proxy/tests/test_slots_model_param_guard.py`.

## Key Files

- `proxy/README.md` — child-port discovery section, model-resolution rule, 400-class table
- `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` — `/slots` 400 semantics section
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `slots_failure_is_definitive_model_absent` to cite
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_model_param_guard.py` — guard test to cite

## Dependencies

- Depends on: LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW (the documented rule must match the implemented resolution order)

## Deliverables

- Updated `proxy/README.md` and `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` documenting the resolution rule and the *missing* / *unknown* / *unloaded* 400 classes.
data.title: Document the model-resolution rule and 400 semantics (AC5 part 2)

# Verify a fresh 24 h router /slots 400 == 0 window (AC4)

**Parent:** LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 · **Slice:** 6 of 6 (post-deploy verification) · **Type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Summary

After deploying slices 3–5 and restarting via `/skill:start-proxy --restart`, measure a fresh 24 h window with the `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` responder split and confirm zero router-responder `GET /slots ... 400` events, attributing anything non-zero.

## Why this slice

AC4 is a production-window signal that cannot be observed inside the implementation session — it starts only after the restart that deploys the fixes. Splitting it out keeps the code slices terminal at `in_review` without pretending AC4 was measured.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC4 — Verification window.** Router-responder `GET /slots ... 400` count is **0** over a fresh 24 h window after deploy + restart, measured with `scripts/slots_500_triage.py`'s responder split and recorded as a comment; any non-zero event must be attributed to the expected unloaded-model class (Q2=A) or an AC1-listed call site — an unexplained event reopens the item.
- [ ] The deployed build is restarted with `/skill:start-proxy --restart` and the window start timestamp is recorded (the window must start at or after that restart).
- [ ] The measurement — command, window start/end, and the router 400 / 500 / 200 plus child 200 counts — is recorded as a comment on the parent item.
- [ ] `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="http_400"}` at window end is recorded alongside the log split.

## Minimal Implementation

- Deploy the merged fixes to `dev` and restart the stack with `/skill:start-proxy --restart`; note the restart time.
- After the 24 h window, run the responder split over `llama-server.log` (and rotated files covering the window) with `scripts/slots_500_triage.py`.
- Snapshot `llama_slots_query_failures_total` from the proxy `/metrics` endpoint.
- Post the measurement comment on LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8; classify any residual event per AC4.

## Key Files

- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` — responder-split measurement tool
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_500_triage.py` — tool behaviour to rely on
- `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` — how to read the split
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — `llama_slots_query_failures_total` metric definition

## Dependencies

- Depends on: LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL (all fixes merged, documented and deployed)

## Deliverables

- One measurement comment on the parent recording a router-responder 400 count of 0 over a fresh 24 h window (or a classified attribution for any residual event).

# Goal

As the operator (and as the producer judging AC1 of the parent measurement), I
want the nightly report to show the full `capacity_hint` distribution — counts
**and** shares, unexpected tokens included — plus the
`saturated`-without-live-work count and shares, so "saturated only with live
work" can be checked straight from `report.md` instead of a standalone tool run.

Parent: **LP-0MVRMHY0F007RWA0** (delivers parent AC2; contributes to parent
AC3/AC4). Builds on the `## Local capacity signals` section skeleton and the
shared `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` module delivered by sibling
`slots_stale rate published end-to-end`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC2.1 (parser).** `status_request` events carry additive `LogEvent` fields
  `local_in_flight_requests`, `local_active_query` and `active_query` (`None` on
  pre-change lines); synthetic schema-2 and schema-3 lines parse to the expected
  values and no other event kind is affected.
- **AC2.2 (single live-work rule).** `has_live_local_work()` lives once in
  `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` — `local_in_flight_requests > 0` when the
  field is present (schema 3, authoritative), else the
  `local_active_query` / `active_query` flags (schema 2 fallback) — and both the
  nightly analyzer and `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` use it.
- **AC2.3 (distribution).** The aggregation reports the `capacity_hint`
  histogram over status polls with **counts and shares**, gives any unexpected
  token its own row rather than dropping or re-bucketing it, and computes the
  `saturated`-without-live-work count with its share of all polls **and** of
  `saturated` polls.
- **AC2.4 (rendering).** The `## Local capacity signals` section renders the
  distribution rows, the saturated-without-live-work rows (count + both shares)
  and a one-line verdict that names each unmet target explicitly instead of
  burying it; the section is still omitted entirely when the window has no
  status polls.
- **AC2.5 (JSON).** `--json` gains additive `capacity_signals.capacity_hint`,
  `capacity_signals.saturated_without_live_work` and `capacity_signals.targets`
  keys mirroring the section; the existing count-only `status_capacity_hint`
  and `denial_attribution.capacity_hint` keys keep their current meaning.
- **AC2.6 (tests).** Tests in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_capacity_signals.py` cover the
  schema-3 authoritative rule versus the schema-2 fallback, an unexpected
  `capacity_hint` token appearing as its own row, shares arithmetic, the empty
  window, the JSON keys, and agreement with `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
  on the same synthetic lines. The full project test suite passes (run through
  the test skill).
- **AC2.7 (honest caveat + coverage note).** The section text repeats the
  reference tool's caveat that the stale rate is a *polling-path* signal
  meaningful only for the build it was measured on, and states when the poll
  figures come from logs that do not span the whole window (or documents the
  limitation explicitly) so a truncated retention window cannot masquerade as a
  complete measurement.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` with the live-work rule plus hint
  histogram / violation helpers (pure, stdlib only); switch
  `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` onto them without changing its
  published figures.

# Goal

Prove the nightly generator reproduces the already-recorded capacity figures for
the 2026-10-24 post-fix night window, so the new report surface is pinned to a
known measurement rather than to its own arithmetic — and so the two
successor re-measurements (LP-0MVRZDC3Y005JHQJ, LP-0MVSTQT8V002SPRZ) can cite
the standard surface instead of another ad-hoc tool run.

Parent: **LP-0MVRMHY0F007RWA0** (delivers parent AC3; reuses parent AC4 and
parent AC1/AC2 behaviour). Reference implementation:
`scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`; recorded artifact:
`~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-24_post-fix-night-measurement/measurement.json`
(`coverage.covered = true`, `window_end_gap_seconds = 2.0`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC3.1 (reproduction of the measured window).** Re-running the analyzer with
  `--start '2026-10-24 20:00:00' --end '2026-10-25 07:00:00'` must reproduce the
  recorded artifact's `capacity_signals` figures: 11,654 status polls; 9,278 stale (79.61 %);
  `capacity_hint` `idle` 4,577 / `prefill_bound` 6,024 / `saturated` 1,053;
  247 saturated-without-live-work. The expected values are a fixture constant
  carrying provenance (artifact path + the commit/work item that recorded it),
  never a re-derived-by-the-same-code value.
- **AC3.2 (real-log run, skip-safe).** The reproduction runs against
  `/var/log/llama-proxy` when that window is retained and is skipped with an
  explicit reason (never silently passed) when it is not; the executed run's
  figures are recorded in a comment on this item.
- **AC3.3 (differences explained, not relaxed).** Every difference from the
  recorded artifact is explained in the work item (boundary semantics, log
  retention, artifact's `window_end_gap_seconds`) — an assertion is never
  loosened to a tolerance without that explanation being recorded first.
- **AC3.4 (boundary semantics test).** A dedicated boundary test asserts a poll
  timestamped exactly at `window_end` is excluded and one exactly at
  `window_start` is included, pinning the half-open semantics the reproduction
  depends on.
- **AC3.5 (no regression of existing surfaces).** The reproduction test
  coexists with the existing suite: the full project test suite passes (run
  through the test skill), and the test file is fast/skippable so an offline CI
  run does not fail on a missing host directory.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the reproduction tests to
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_capacity_signals.py` (fixture
  constant + `pytest.mark.skipif` on the host log directory / window
  retention), plus the boundary test.
- Execute the two documented verification commands from the parent description
  once, compare the figures, and record both outputs (and the comparison) in a
  comment on this item.
- Document any difference and its cause in the work item before touching an
  assertion.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_capacity_signals.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` (only if a genuine
  semantic gap is found — no speculative change)
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` (reference surface for the
  comparison)

## Method

Verification-first: the test and the recorded comparison exist before any
production adjustment; if the figures disagree, the cause is diagnosed (not
papered over) and, where the cause is a real defect in the new slices, a
blocking child item is filed against this item.

## Risks

- **Retention** — the window may age out of `/var/log/llama-proxy`; the skip path
  (AC3.2) keeps the suite green while AC3.3 records the limitation honestly.
- **Boundary drift** — the analyzer's legacy inclusive-end aggregation must not
  leak into the status-poll path; AC3.4 is the guard.
- **Fixture rot** — pinning a value also pins a log-era schema; the fixture
  names the schema version and the artifact commit so a future re-baseline is
  deliberate.

## Deliverables

Reproduction + boundary tests, the recorded real-log comparison, and an explicit
statement in this item of "reproduced exactly" or "differs because …".

Redefine `remote-ok` to *"local allowed, remote acceptable"*: it keeps the local route and never waits for a slot (parent AC15, AC16, AC20). This child lands **before** the default inversion so the suite stays green - today `remote-ok` is a non-default value, so changing its meaning breaks no headerless caller.

## Goal

Make the value that will become the default safe to be the default: it attempts local when a slot is free, and steps straight to the next provider in the chain when local cannot serve the request right now - no queue entry, no deferral, no local-capacity `429`.

## Scope

- `apply_local_preference()` loses `strip_by_preference`; the capacity strip (`CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`) and its remote-less carve-out are kept byte-identical, so no preference can empty a chain.
- Remove (or neutralise) both dead `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK: ... "providers": []` branches in the two dispatch cycles.
- `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` declines to enqueue for `remote-ok`, returning the `"fallback_policy"`-equivalent outcome so the caller falls through immediately.
- Docstrings for `apply_local_preference`, `local_preference_for_request` and `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` state the new meaning and the historic-name warning.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`: the preference-table row for `remote-ok` and the per-exit fall-through notes that describe the strip are re-anchored on the capacity strip alone (no preference-based strip exists any more).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (no preference strip: `remote-ok` keeps the local route, parent AC15).** `apply_local_preference()` (`priority.py:459-474`) no longer filters on `preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK`: the only preference-independent strip that remains is the capacity strip (`verdict == CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`), with its existing remote-less carve-out. `remote-ok` therefore means *"local allowed, remote acceptable"*: the local entry stays in the chain and is attempted exactly as a headerless request attempts it today. A test row asserts a `remote-ok` request attempts local (the upstream calls include the local provider, `X-Local-Route: local`) when local can serve, and that `PREF_REMOTE_OK` produces no `providers`-stripping in `effective_chain_for_request()`.
- **AC3 (no preference can empty a chain, parent AC16).** The `private` model + explicit `remote-ok` is served locally (200, zero remote calls); the `private` model + absent header is unchanged at this stage; a normal chain with local down serves from the next remote entry, and exhaustion only when nothing is left to try. The two dead empty-chain branches are gone (grep-asserted). **Restates parent AC16:** Removing the preference strip makes the empty-chain hazard disappear rather than moving it: `apply_local_preference()` can only strip for capacity, and that strip already returns a remote-less chain intact (`priority.py:470-474`). Two branches that exist only to serve the old `remote-ok`-strips-everything behaviour must be removed or neutralised: the `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK: … providers: []` fallbacks in both dispatch cycles (`provider.py:11445`, `:12142` as of 2026-10-30). Test rows: (a) `private` model (single `type: local` provider, `config.yaml:400-408`) + absent header ⇒ 200 served **locally**, no exhaustion body, zero remote calls; (b) `private` model + explicit `remote-ok` ⇒ same; (c) `remote-ok` on a normal chain with local down ⇒ the next remote entry serves (exhaustion only when there is genuinely nothing left to try).
- **AC4 (immediate step, no queue, parent AC20).** For each local-exit cause enumerated in parent AC20 (slot saturated, prefill-ETA over budget, local cooldown, residency/thrash skip, lease held, per-entry context cap) a `remote-ok` request produces `X-Local-Route: remote`, a `contention_queue` wait of 0, and exactly one upstream call. `high` priority keeps its existing never-queue semantics.
- **AC5 (documentation matches, parent AC12 slice).** `routing.md` no longer states that `remote-ok` removes the local route, the historic-name warning is present, and the pinned exit-table docs test (`test_local_only_exit_docs.py`) passes with the re-anchored `too_large` rows.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Delete the preference strip in `apply_local_preference()`; keep the capacity strip and carve-out untouched.
2. Delete the two `PREF_REMOTE_OK` empty-chain branches.
3. Add the `remote-ok` early decline in `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` (before the reservation/ticket handling so no ticket is consumed for a request that will not wait).
4. Update the three docstrings and the `routing.md` rows.
5. Fill in the `remote-ok` rows of the contract specs from the previous child.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the contract-test child.

data.description:
Make `remote-ok` the default and retire `prefer-local` with the same loud `400` (parent AC14, AC17, AC18, AC19, AC21, AC9). The default flip and the `prefer-local` retirement must land **together**: retiring the current default first would break every headerless caller, and flipping the default first would leave a silent reinterpretation path.

## Goal

One written, observable vocabulary policy: exactly two live values, `remote-ok` as the default, and a headerless client that never waits for a slot it did not ask for.

## Scope

- `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE = PREF_REMOTE_OK`; `VALID_PREFERENCES == (PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED, PREF_REMOTE_OK)`.
- `prefer-local` rejected through the retirement mechanism from the earlier child, with a `detail` naming both live values - never silently resolved to the new default (an explicit `prefer-local` asked to *wait*; the default does not).
- Exactly one startup log line naming the active default and the retired values; routing lines keep reporting the resolved preference with no new key.
- Test sweep: every module relying on the implicit `prefer-local` default sets the header explicitly, including `PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES` (drop `LOCAL_ONLY`) and the absent-header parameter lists; the vocabulary tests assert the two-value set **and** the new default.
- Document the expected behaviour shift (no queue wait by default; opportunistic local serving) so the daily usage report's local/remote split is not later read as a local-serving regression. No skill or report file is edited (repository boundary).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_routing_preference_logging.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (two live values, parent AC21).** `VALID_PREFERENCES` is exactly the two-value tuple, `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE == remote-ok`, and an absent header resolves to `remote-ok` and inherits the keep-local/no-queue behaviour. **Restates parent AC21:** `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE = PREF_REMOTE_OK`, so an **absent header** and any genuinely unknown value resolve to `remote-ok` and inherit AC15 + AC20. `VALID_PREFERENCES == (PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED, PREF_REMOTE_OK)` — exactly two live values. The knock-on surface is stated for the reader, because it is now the *default* path rather than a niche value: the prefill-ETA admission guard still runs (it decides whether local can serve now) but its **refusal** outcome is unreachable for this preference, and the contention queue, the deferral/retry surface and `POST /llama/local/reserve` are reachable only for `local-preferred` clients.
- **AC2 (prefer-local retired loudly, parent AC14).** An explicit `X-Local-Preference: prefer-local` returns `400`, `code: local_preference_retired`, `detail` naming `local-preferred` and `remote-ok`; it is never resolved to the new default; zero upstream calls. **Restates parent AC14:** `prefer-local` leaves `VALID_PREFERENCES`. An **explicit** `X-Local-Preference: prefer-local` is rejected with the same stable shape as AC1 (`400`, `code: local_preference_retired`, a `detail` naming `local-preferred` and `remote-ok`) rather than being silently resolved to the new default. Rationale is symmetric to AC1: an explicit `prefer-local` means "wait for local when it fits the wait budget", while the new default `remote-ok` means "take local only when it is free right now" — silently reinterpreting it would deliver a materially different policy with no signal, and a client relying on the queue wait would silently start paying for remote dispatch.
- **AC3 (default observable, parent AC17).** Exactly one startup line names the active default and the retired values; a headerless request's routing line reports `preference=remote-ok` with no new log key. **Restates parent AC17:** Exactly one log line at startup (or on the first dispatch) names the active `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE` and the retired values, so an operator can prove from `proxy.log` which vocabulary policy the *running* proxy applies — a deploy that ships the code without the intended config is otherwise invisible. Routing lines keep reporting the resolved preference with no new key (`preference=remote-ok` for headerless requests).
- **AC4 (test sweep, parent AC19).** Every test that depended on the implicit default sets the header explicitly (grep-driven sweep of the modules listed in the parent's existing-state section; the parent's "~55 occurrences / 16 modules" figure is stale - current grep shows 8 test modules and 69 occurrences including sources, so the sweep is grep-driven, not count-driven); `PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES` drops `LOCAL_ONLY`; the vocabulary tests pin both the set and the default so a silent revert fails. **Restates parent AC19:** Every test that relied on the implicit `prefer-local` default sets the header explicitly (grep-driven: the plan-time count is 8 test modules plus 2 source modules, 69 occurrences of `prefer-local` in `proxy/tests` + `proxy/proxy` outside `__pycache__`, verified 2026-10-30 — an earlier "16 modules / ~55 occurrences" figure counted a wider tree, so sweep by grep, not by count), including the pin-local parameter lists that still carry the retired spelling (`PIN_LOCAL_PREFERENCES = (LOCAL_ONLY, LOCAL_PREFERRED)`, `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py:592`, which must drop `LOCAL_ONLY`), and the vocabulary tests assert the two-value set **and** the new default so a silent revert fails.
- **AC5 (post-inversion intent matrix, parent AC9).** The matrix rows are stated in the two-value vocabulary: `local-preferred` is the only pin-local value (escalation applies to every pinned request; a remote-less chain keeps refusing), `remote-ok` asserts its two new observables rather than "unchanged", and both retired values assert `400`.
- **AC6 (shift documented, parent AC18).** `routing.md` records the two expected shifts - no queue wait by default (`contention_queue_*` lines disappear for headerless traffic) and opportunistic local serving - and the completion comment repeats them so the daily report's change is not misread as a regression. **Restates parent AC18:** The item records the two shifts: (a) **no queue wait by default** — `contention_queue_dispatch` / `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` lines disappear for headerless traffic, so the measured `queued_duration` median drops to ~0 and the remote share rises whenever the GPU is busy at request time; (b) local serving is now **opportunistic** — a headerless request is served locally only when a slot is free at that instant, so local utilisation falls and `X-Local-Route: remote` with a fall-through reason becomes the common outcome under contention. No skill or report file is edited (repository boundary); the expectation is stated in `proxy/docs/routing.md` and in the completion comment so the daily proxy-usage report's shift is not mistaken for a local-serving defect.
- **AC7 (no remote-less regression, parent AC16).** The `private` model serves locally under an absent header (200, zero remote calls, no exhaustion body) - the highest-severity hazard of the inversion, asserted at the flip.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Flip `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE`, drop `prefer-local` from the live set and register it as retired with both successors.
2. Grep-driven sweep: set explicit headers in the affected tests, drop retired values from parameter lists.
3. Add the startup line (one emission per process) and assert it once.
4. Update the preference table, the "unknown values behave as `prefer-local`" paragraph and the metric-shift note in `routing.md` and `config.yaml`.
5. Turn the remaining contract specs green.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the contract-test child, the `remote-ok` semantics child (the new default must already be safe) and the `local-only` retirement child (the mechanism is shared).

data.description:
Final slice: rewrite the client-facing documentation and guidance against the live vocabulary, migrate the one in-repo caller, and pin both with docs-contract tests so a future retirement cannot leave stale advice behind (parent AC12, AC22, AC13).

## Goal

A reader (and a client) can discover the two live values, the `400` shapes, the immediate-step contract and the bounded-deferral contract from `routing.md`/`config.yaml`/the refusal body - and a test fails if any of them drifts from the implementation.

## Scope

- `proxy/docs/routing.md`: replace the three-value preference table, the wire-compatibility paragraph, the "unknown values behave as `prefer-local`" line, the "clients may keep sending `local-only`" paragraph and the per-exit fall-through notes with the two-value table (`remote-ok` marked as the default and as "local allowed, remote acceptable"), both retirement `400` shapes, the immediate-step contract and the bounded-deferral contract (exact fields, headers, token).
- `too_large` rows that describe "the same filter `remote-ok` uses" are re-anchored on the capacity strip alone.
- `proxy/config.yaml` commentary: two values, the new default, the immediate-step semantics, and the legacy-alias text replaced; `local_deferral_max_refusals` documented.
- Code docstrings: `parse_preference`, `local_preference_for_request`, `apply_local_preference`, `_local_preference_pins_local`, `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot`, the refusal builders and the module docstring vocabulary paragraph.
- `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` must name `remote-ok` (it currently advises the retired `prefer-local`); coordinate with the open item LP-0MVTGI2RP009SRKN so the rebase preserves a live value.
- `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py` (the only in-repo sender of a retired value) moves both sends to `local-preferred`; historical incident narrative in `docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md` is left as written.
- Docs-contract tests pin the documented values, default and token against the implementation, and keep the escalation prose outside the ranges pinned by `test_local_only_exit_docs.py` (Risk R4).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_retry_docs.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_fallback_reason_tokens.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (routing docs, parent AC12).** `routing.md` contains no claim that `remote-ok` removes the local route, no `prefer-local` default row, no "clients may keep sending `local-only`" paragraph, and no statement that unknown values behave as `prefer-local`; it documents the two live values, both `400` shapes, the immediate-step contract and the deferral-budget contract with their exact headers and token. **Restates parent AC12:** `proxy/docs/routing.md` is updated: the preference table (`:1355` `prefer-local` default row, `:1359` wire-compatibility paragraph, `:1367` "unknown values behave as `prefer-local`"), the per-exit fallthrough notes (`:1484`, `:1613`, `:1717`, `:1729`) and the "clients may keep sending `local-only`" paragraph (`:1567`) are replaced with the two-value table (`local-preferred`, `remote-ok` **as the default**, with the historic-name warning of AC15's constraint), both retirements and their `400` shapes, and the immediate-step contract (AC20); the `too_large` rows that describe "the same filter `remote-ok` uses" (`:1385`, `:1502-1504`, `:1598`) are re-anchored on the capacity strip alone, since that filter no longer exists; the `local-preferred` section (`:1345`-ish, which currently states the proxy "never silently promotes") gains the bounded-deferral contract with the exact fields, headers and escalation token a client must honour. `proxy/config.yaml` commentary naming the legacy alias and the three-value vocabulary (`:1929-1953`) is rewritten to the two values, the new default and the immediate-step semantics. Code docstrings for `parse_preference`, `local_preference_for_request`, `apply_local_preference`, `_local_preference_pins_local`, `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` and the refusal builders are updated to match. The one client-facing string that names a retired value must change with them: `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` (`provider.py:4710-4713`, "…or send X-Local-Preference: prefer-local to allow a remote fallback") currently advises a value that will `400` — it must name `remote-ok`, and the rebase with LP-0MVTGI2RP009SRKN (which rewrites that string) must preserve the live value. A docs-contract test pins the guidance against the live vocabulary so a future retirement cannot leave stale advice behind.
- **AC2 (docs-contract tests, parent AC12/Risk R4).** A test ties the documented values, default, immediate-step contract and `deferral_refusals_exhausted` token to the implementation and fails if any recorded value is not in the live vocabulary; the escalation prose sits outside the ranges pinned by `test_local_only_exit_docs.py`, whose pinned assertion still passes.
- **AC3 (client-facing guidance, parent AC12).** `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` names a live value (`remote-ok`) and a test pins it against the live vocabulary so a future retirement cannot leave stale advice; the LP-0MVTGI2RP009SRKN interaction is recorded (rebase, not duplicate prose) in the completion comment.
- **AC4 (in-repo caller migrated, parent AC22).** Both sends in `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py` use `local-preferred`; a grep over `*.py`/`*.yaml`/`*.md`/`*.sh`/`*.ts` (excluding `.worklog`, worktrees, `__pycache__`) finds no non-test sender of a retired value; the historical narrative in `docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md` is unchanged. **Restates parent AC22:** The only in-repo sender of a retired value is the verification harness `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py` (`:587` `"X-Local-Preference": "prefer-local"`, `:649` `"local-only"` — verified 2026-10-30; no other non-test sender exists in the tree). Both move to `local-preferred`, because both scenarios verify local serving/admission behaviour and need the pin-local semantics; a run of the harness against a proxy built from this change must not receive a `400`. Historical narrative that quotes the old values as part of the incident record (`docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md:37`, `:180`) is **left as written** — it describes what happened, not what to send.
- **AC5 (gate, parent AC13).** The changed-scope test gate is green before commit; the full suite is left to the dev-push gate. Complete the work item with the commit message and hash recorded in a comment.

## Minimal Implementation
